uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly consumer price index, the measure the Bank of England targets at 2%. It feeds into rate decisions, wage settlements and benefit uprating, and sterling and gilt yields move on it.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The September figure is the one UK benefit uprating is set against, so this release settles more than a monthly reading: it fixes next year's increase for most working-age benefits as well as showing where consumer prices stood through September.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate target. Its decisions set the cost of dollar borrowing worldwide, from US mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-10.recent: In September the committee voted 12-0 to raise rates, defying Trump's calls to lower them, and the cause was a closed strait that had pushed Brent crude near $110 a barrel. This meeting settles whether the Fed keeps tightening into a supply shock it cannot reach, with the cost landing on households already paying more for fuel.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council sets interest rates for every country that uses the euro, meeting about every six weeks. Its decisions set borrowing costs across the eurozone and move the euro and European government bonds.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The European Central Bank meets after the Fed raised rates 12-0 over a closed strait and the Bank of Japan took its rate to a 31-year high, with Brent near $110 a barrel. This decision settles whether Frankfurt joins them in tightening into the same supply shock or holds.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions move the yen and Japanese government bond yields, and reach capital that Japanese savers have invested around the world.
boj-2026-10.recent: The Bank of Japan's September hike took its rate to a 31-year high to curb rising prices, so this meeting will show whether that was a single step or the start of a sustained run. Every move also runs through the BOJ's balancing act with Bessent, which has only grown harder.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who meet eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its decisions pass quickly into UK mortgage costs, and sterling moves with them.
boe-2026-11.recent: The Bank of England decides after the Fed and the Bank of Japan both raised rates in September, with Brent near $106 a barrel pushing an oil shock into prices. This meeting settles whether London also tightens into that supply shock or holds.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate. Its decisions set the price of dollar credit worldwide, from US mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The Fed's September hike passed 12-0, against Trump's calls to lower rates, and its cause was a closed strait, a supply shock that no interest rate can reopen. US consumer prices rose 0.4% in August as the war reached the price index. This meeting settles whether that hike was a single answer to imported inflation or the start of a tightening run.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The Group of Twenty brings together 19 of the largest economies plus the European Union and African Union. Its leaders meet once a year under a rotating presidency, and together they account for most of the world's output and trade.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Rubio has invited Vladimir Putin, who is wanted by the ICC, to Miami in December, and Zelensky has said he is willing to meet him there. That makes the host's guest list the summit's first question. Alongside it sits the Trump-Xi summit, which was shaped by Washington's caps on Nvidia's compute sales to China.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council sets interest rates for every country that uses the euro, meeting about every six weeks. Its decisions reach mortgages, business loans and government borrowing across the bloc, and the euro moves with them.
ecb-2026-12.recent: The European Central Bank's rate decision sets what banks pay to borrow from it and what they earn on money parked with it for the months after. Nothing reported so far makes this meeting different from a routine one.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate, the rate it pays on reserves. Its decisions reach UK mortgages, savings and business loans, and sterling moves with them.
boe-2026-12.recent: The Bank of England's committee decides where its policy rate sits. That sets the cost of borrowing and the return on savings until its next meeting.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's Policy Board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. After decades near zero, its decisions reach Japanese savers and borrowers, the yen, and the global trades funded in it.
boj-2026-12.recent: The Bank of Japan raised its rate to a 31-year high in September to curb rising prices, and this meeting weighs whether that pressure still calls for tightening. It weighs it inside a balancing act with Bessent in Washington that has only grown harder, while the Fed has been raising rates into a supply shock from a closed strait.

fred-us-gdp-2026-09-30.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's measure of US gross domestic product, published each quarter in three successive estimates. It is the broadest gauge of the world's largest economy, and it feeds rate policy, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-gdp-2026-09-30.recent: Last week the OECD said AI investment is carrying the U.S. economy faster than its allies and offsetting the Middle East energy shock for now, as the Nasdaq hit an all-time high. This release tests that claim against official output data: how much of the growth is AI spending, and how much is left once it is set aside.

fred-us-pce-2026-09-30.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on US personal income, consumer spending and the PCE price index. The Federal Reserve targets that index at 2%, so each reading feeds directly into rate expectations.
fred-us-pce-2026-09-30.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes the latest US PCE reading, which settles how fast consumer prices rose last month and whether household spending kept pace.

fred-us-jobs-report-2026-10-02.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly employment report, usually out on the first Friday, counts jobs added and the unemployment rate. It moves Treasury yields, the dollar and expectations for Federal Reserve policy.
fred-us-jobs-report-2026-10-02.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the US jobs report, the first full read on last month's hiring and unemployment. It will settle how the labour market ended the month.
